correctness.rationale: Under normalized probability measure on S^2 the degree-l projector kernel has diagonal 2l+1 and vanishing one-point mean. Centering leaves 2/n times the unordered sample-edge sum. In the second moment only repeated edges remain, with integral delta_(l,m)d_l. In the cubic expansion a degree-one vertex kills a term; three identical edges and triangles on three distinct sample points are the only surviving multigraphs. There are binomial(n,2) of the former and 6 binomial(n,3) labeled edge assignments of the latter. A repeated edge integrates to d_l d_m d_k times the Gaunt square since X dot Y is uniform on [-1,1]; the triangle is the trace of the product of three harmonic projections, nonzero only for all equal degrees and then equal to d_l. These quantities and (2/n)^3 recover the stated normalization. The zero-row Wigner factorial has precisely the parity and triangle support, including degenerate triangles. Direct integration of the two low-degree products gives G_123=9 and G_112=6. The covariance of the squared centered energy with another energy is the corresponding repeated-degree cumulant. Its strict positivity, like the mixed selection statement, is for n>=2; at n=1 all centered moments vanish. The package checker was inspected, not run: its icosahedral samples check selected degree-1/2 moments only (degree at most four per sample coordinate), with floating tolerance, not arbitrary harmonic degrees or n. The general proof does not rest on that evidence.

value.rationale: Distinct harmonic energies are uncorrelated, but this exact all-degree law identifies which pairs and triples still have cubic dependence before the asymptotic independent chi-square regime. Finite-sample null dependence is naturally relevant to combining harmonic uniformity tests. The scope is cubic moments, not the full distribution, new critical values, or a power claim.
